findings.title: Main Chat privacy route and raw LifeModel claim diverge from wire behavior
findings.root_cause: The scheduler and LLM layer can rebuild a full LifeModel prompt after the kernel records that raw YAML was excluded, and direct generation does not share one persisted privacy decision.
findings.reproduction: Capture the provider request for a sensitive direct-answer turn and compare it with kernel raw_life_model_yaml_included metadata.
findings.acceptance: No provider request contains raw LifeModel YAML and the execution receipt matches the captured request.
findings.deletion_target: Scheduler and LLM call signatures that accept LifeModel for ordinary generation

findings.title: MCP registration IPC permits arbitrary local code execution
findings.root_cause: A shipped command accepts arbitrary arguments and environment for interpreters such as node and python, so the executable-name allowlist does not constrain code execution.
findings.owner_module: Release capability contract and MCP runtime
findings.reproduction: Inspect the shipped handler and register python -c or node -e arguments in an isolated test profile.
findings.acceptance: Release has no arbitrary registration command; only immutable bundled or authenticated remote MCP contracts may later re-enter the product.
findings.deletion_target: register_mcp_server and unregister_mcp_server release handler entries

findings.title: Reversed global lock order can deadlock the process
findings.root_cause: Main Chat and generic execution acquire permission, registry, and audit locks in different orders and hold some guards across external awaits.
findings.reproduction: Use barriers to run the two opposite acquisition paths concurrently and retain task dumps on timeout.
findings.acceptance: No external await holds shared store guards and 10000 concurrent interleavings complete without deadlock.
findings.deletion_target: Nested AppState mutex acquisition helpers used across external calls

findings.title: Streaming waits for the full answer and emits one reply chunk
findings.root_cause: The streaming wrapper awaits the buffered turn result instead of consuming a provider token stream owned by the turn runtime.
findings.reproduction: Run a delayed token fixture and record event arrival timestamps.
findings.acceptance: Provider tokens arrive incrementally and send collects the same event stream without a second runtime.
findings.deletion_target: Single whole-reply chunk emission after buffered completion

findings.title: Errors leave running tasks and cancellation does not stop live work
findings.root_cause: Task creation precedes fallible execution but no universal terminal finalizer or live cancellation registry owns every exit path.
findings.reproduction: Force provider timeout and cancel a blocked provider while observing task and late-write state.
findings.acceptance: Every exit is terminal, local cancellation completes within the gate, and no durable write arrives after cancellation.
findings.deletion_target: Database-only cancellation and question-mark error exits after task creation

findings.title: Stable 32-bit task identifiers reuse completed work
findings.root_cause: Task identity is derived from a collision-prone prompt hash and resume accepts an existing terminal task.
findings.reproduction: Send the same prompt twice in one session and compare task ids and transcripts.
findings.acceptance: Each logical run uses UUIDv4 and repeated prompts have independent task state.
findings.deletion_target: FNV prompt-derived task id generation

findings.title: AllowOnce permission can be consumed concurrently
findings.root_cause: Permission selection and consumption are separate operations and the update lacks a consumed_at compare-and-swap predicate.
findings.reproduction: Synchronize 100 consumers on one AllowOnce record.
findings.acceptance: A single conditional update permits exactly one local consumer.
findings.deletion_target: Find-then-consume AllowOnce sequence

findings.title: Concurrent proposal acceptance can duplicate side effects
findings.root_cause: Acceptance reads Pending, performs the effect, and only then stores Accepted without an atomic dispatch claim.
findings.reproduction: Accept one proposal concurrently through a counting fake effect adapter.
findings.acceptance: Only one request acquires the local dispatch claim; ambiguous remote effects become unknown rather than replayed.
findings.deletion_target: Apply-before-status-transition acceptance path

findings.title: LifeModel baseline check and commit permit lost updates
findings.root_cause: The manager lock is released between base validation and final write so two proposals can pass the same baseline.
findings.reproduction: Apply two patches with the same base version behind a barrier.
findings.acceptance: One versioned CAS commits and the other produces an inspectable conflict.
findings.deletion_target: Split baseline-check and write critical sections

findings.title: Generic execute_tool_call is a second execution authority
findings.root_cause: The shipped IPC constructs a partial action context outside the Main Chat ToolGateway governance and claims unsanitized inputs are sanitized.
findings.reproduction: Compare direct IPC execution context and evidence with the governed Main Chat path.
findings.acceptance: The release handler has no generic direct execution command and every product tool call enters ToolGateway.
findings.deletion_target: execute_tool_call release handler and direct execution body

findings.title: ActionExecutor cloud and timeout configuration is inert
findings.root_cause: allow_cloud and timeout_seconds are carried as data but not enforced around provider or tool operations.
findings.reproduction: Set cloud deny and a short timeout against adapters that would otherwise execute or hang.
findings.acceptance: Denied cloud calls never start and hung calls reach a structured timeout state.
findings.deletion_target: Unused execution configuration fields

findings.title: Scheduler is sequential, running state is volatile, and snapshot rewrite loses tasks
findings.root_cause: The runner reads and rewrites a whole JSON snapshot, marks running only in memory, and does not share writer coordination.
findings.reproduction: Add a task during a blocked run and crash after external dispatch before final rewrite.
findings.acceptance: Durable claim and lease preserve new tasks and ambiguous effects require reconciliation.
findings.deletion_target: Whole-file sequential scheduler runner

findings.title: A2A starts automatically without authentication and exposes LifeModel data
findings.root_cause: Startup launches a loopback server whose task and AgentCard endpoints trust any local caller and use a fresh default privacy engine.
findings.reproduction: Start release and query the task endpoint from an unrelated local process.
findings.acceptance: Release does not autostart A2A; re-enabled private endpoints require pairing and use persisted policy.
findings.deletion_target: Unconditional A2A setup launch and unauthenticated routes

findings.title: A2A outbound accepts arbitrary URL and raw payload
findings.root_cause: Direct commands bypass network policy, private-address checks, authentication, privacy selection, timeout, and response limits.
findings.reproduction: Send a task to a private redirect target and capture the raw payload.
findings.acceptance: Outbound A2A uses HTTPS, declared authentication, network policy, and ContextManifest minimization.
findings.deletion_target: Direct A2AClient command calls

findings.title: Web SSRF checks do not cover redirects, DNS changes, or large bodies
findings.root_cause: Only the initial URL is validated, domain matching uses suffix text, reqwest follows redirects, and the full body is loaded before truncation.
findings.reproduction: Redirect a public URL to loopback, use a suffix-confusion domain, and return an oversized response.
findings.acceptance: Every hop and pinned address is valid, DNS labels match exactly, and streaming size limits fail closed.
findings.deletion_target: Initial-URL-only private check and host.ends_with policy

findings.title: NetworkPolicy ask has no execution semantics
findings.root_cause: The executor checks enabled and deny lists but ignores default ask and per-domain ask decisions.
findings.reproduction: Configure default ask and execute a network read without an existing grant.
findings.acceptance: Ask creates an explicit consent state and no network request starts first.
findings.deletion_target: Boolean-only network policy enforcement

findings.title: ModelRouter behavior changes after saving the same config
findings.root_cause: Bootstrap omits the router, save_config attaches one, availability uses a separate cache, and local providers are not seeded consistently.
findings.reproduction: Compare route decisions before save, after save, and after restart with identical config.
findings.acceptance: All three decisions and availability evidence match.
findings.deletion_target: Scheduler optional router and parallel provider health authority

findings.title: Missing API key is returned as a successful model answer
findings.root_cause: The provider adapter returns Ok with user-facing text and downstream code equates non-empty Ok with generation success.
findings.reproduction: Select a cloud provider without a key and inspect final delivery and generation evidence.
findings.acceptance: The turn reports structured provider_unconfigured failure and no model-generated credit.
findings.deletion_target: Missing-key success string

findings.title: MCP audit encryption and rotation do not provide the claimed key semantics
findings.root_cause: Keys derive from public constants, passphrase mode has no passphrase, missing env uses empty input, and epoch changes do not change the key.
findings.reproduction: Rotate epochs and compare derived keys and decryptability without secret material.
findings.acceptance: Random keychain keys differ by epoch and initialization or decryption failure is visible.
findings.deletion_target: Constant-derived audit key modes and ignored init error

findings.title: Separate SQLite and file stores permit partial commit and split-brain fallback
findings.root_cause: Canonical and derived writes are sequenced across stores while each store independently falls back to temporary or in-memory state.
findings.reproduction: Fail each write boundary and canonical store initialization while inspecting all stores.
findings.acceptance: Canonical transaction plus outbox commits atomically; projection lag is explicit and release does not silently change storage authority.
findings.deletion_target: Product durable temp/in-memory fallback and cross-store imperative write sequence

findings.title: External MCP uses blocking unbounded IO while holding shared registry state
findings.root_cause: The client uses blocking process read_line without timeout or frame limit and registry operations probe live servers under a global lock.
findings.reproduction: Register a server that never terminates a line and list manifests concurrently.
findings.acceptance: Async framed IO times out, oversized frames disconnect, and other servers remain available.
findings.deletion_target: Blocking MCP client and lock-held live probing

findings.title: AgentRun duplicates raw user input and reasoning traces
findings.root_cause: Run persistence stores full user input and trace payloads instead of referencing canonical conversation and action records.
findings.reproduction: Inspect one completed chat across conversation, AgentRun, event, and audit stores.
findings.acceptance: AgentRun and events contain references, digests, bounded summaries, and no duplicate raw message.
findings.deletion_target: AgentRun raw user_input and unbounded trace persistence

findings.title: Danger-action confirmation evidence is client-forgeable and replayable
findings.root_cause: Confirmation identifiers and phrases are deterministic client fields with no trusted interaction, expiry, or one-time server state.
findings.reproduction: Construct the advertised phrase and digest without displaying the product confirmation UI.
findings.acceptance: Privileged actions require trusted native confirmation and scoped one-time server state.
findings.deletion_target: Deterministic confirmation phrase contract

findings.title: Vector search and rebuild block interaction as data grows
findings.root_cause: Search decodes and sorts JSON vectors under a lock and rebuild embeds every message sequentially without cancellation or checkpointing.
findings.reproduction: Benchmark 20000 vectors and cancel a large rebuild.
findings.acceptance: Binary vectors, bounded top-k, lock-free compute, batching, progress, cancellation, and resume meet the frozen benchmark.
findings.deletion_target: Locked JSON full scan and sequential all-history rebuild

findings.title: PolicyRouter and Kernel are dual intent authorities
findings.root_cause: A broad lexical router selects a strategy and the kernel independently reclassifies action and governance intent.
findings.reproduction: Use prompts whose substrings route differently from their semantic request and compare both decisions.
findings.acceptance: Only PolicyRouter selects the product action; model assistance cannot lower deterministic risk.
findings.deletion_target: Kernel product-route classifiers and direct keyword strategy decisions

findings.title: Event order and runtime status contain hard-coded or inferred facts
findings.root_cause: Done is emitted before durable events and observed AgentLoop/provider fields are set from code-path assumptions rather than adapter facts.
findings.reproduction: Compare event order and status fields with actual tool/provider adapter invocations.
findings.acceptance: Durable terminal facts persist before final and unobserved facts remain unknown.
findings.deletion_target: Hard-coded observed flags and pre-durable done event

findings.title: Shipped command surface and God modules remain oversized
findings.root_cause: Retired commands remain registered as fail-closed shells and core responsibilities accumulate in a few files without deep interfaces.
findings.owner_module: Phase7 deletion manifest and deep runtime modules
findings.reproduction: Inventory shipped handler entries and module line/responsibility counts.
findings.acceptance: Retired shells are absent and deletion tests show complexity concentrated behind deep interfaces.
findings.deletion_target: Retired shipped commands and shallow helper routes

findings.title: Strict workspace Clippy gate fails
findings.root_cause: Warnings and structural lint debt are allowed to accumulate across production and test targets.
findings.reproduction: Run cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings.
findings.acceptance: The strict command exits zero without broad allow attributes.
findings.deletion_target: Known Clippy warnings and gate exceptions

findings.title: Dependency audit carries allowed unsound and unmaintained warnings
findings.root_cause: Advisories are allowlisted without a shipped-target reachability and upgrade disposition gate.
findings.reproduction: Run cargo audit and resolve each warning through cargo tree for shipped targets.
findings.acceptance: Every advisory is fixed, proven unreachable, or has an explicit owner and expiry; no unreviewed shipped unsound issue remains.
findings.deletion_target: Unowned advisory allowlist entries

findings.title: Full Tauri suite has load-sensitive stream timeout
findings.root_cause: Buffered pseudo-streaming, long-held locks, and fixed total timeout make the test sensitive to suite load.
findings.reproduction: Run the full Tauri suite and the isolated clarification stream test with timing evidence.
findings.acceptance: The focused case passes ten times and the full suite passes three consecutive runs.
findings.deletion_target: Fixed whole-turn stream timeout path

findings.title: Source-string tests are treated as behavior evidence
findings.root_cause: Deletion guards and source contains assertions are reused to claim concurrency, network, cancellation, and capability correctness.
findings.reproduction: Classify source-reading tests by absence guard versus behavior claim.
findings.acceptance: Source scans only prove absence/ownership; behavior claims use interfaces and real state or adapter evidence.
findings.deletion_target: Behavior readiness claims backed only by source strings

findings.title: External MCP manifests lack executable risk and action contracts
findings.root_cause: Dynamic manifests contain empty permission, risk, action, and capability fields, so the gateway correctly rejects most product execution.
findings.reproduction: Register a real external MCP tool and validate it through ToolGateway.
findings.acceptance: Only complete typed manifests execute and incomplete manifests fail closed with actionable diagnostics.
findings.deletion_target: Empty or name-inferred MCP execution contracts

findings.title: Provider and search keys are written in plaintext config
findings.root_cause: AppConfig serializes secret values together with ordinary settings instead of referencing OS-protected secret storage.
findings.reproduction: Save provider configuration and inspect the app config file.
findings.acceptance: Config contains only secret references and keychain failure never falls back to plaintext.
findings.deletion_target: Serialized API key fields in AppConfig persistence

findings.title: Blocking tools simulate async with thread spawn followed by join
findings.root_cause: Worker threads are created and synchronously joined, so the caller remains blocked and pays unbounded thread overhead.
findings.reproduction: Use a blocked web or A2A adapter and inspect caller progress and thread count.
findings.acceptance: No immediate join or per-call runtime remains; blocking work is bounded and cancellable.
findings.deletion_target: spawn-then-join and per-call Tokio runtime helpers

findings.title: Model selection and database migration silently substitute or ignore failure
findings.root_cause: Missing configured local models fall back to the first installed model and multiple schema ALTER or initialization errors are discarded.
findings.reproduction: Configure a missing model and inject migration errors while observing reported state.
findings.acceptance: The model is explicitly unavailable, migrations are versioned transactions, and errors produce degraded or failed state rather than silent replacement.
findings.deletion_target: First-installed-model fallback and ignored migration errors
